key_insight: DMAIC combined with FMEA pinpoints the most critical SMAW training defects, showing that a structured quality-improvement workflow can substantially target the main sources of welding error.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a practical, risk-based framework for improving welding instruction, reducing waste, and strengthening shop-floor readiness in technical institutions.
method: Applied Six Sigma DMAIC to assess and improve SMAW training quality.
Used FMEA to rank defect modes by risk priority number (RPN).
Compared defect patterns across two technical institutions in Imo State, Nigeria.
evidence_signal: From 87 recorded defects, lack of fusion was most common (25.29%), followed by undercut (22.99%) and porosity (21.84%), while FMEA assigned the highest RPNs to lack of fusion (245) and porosity (240).
watch_item: The improvement plan depends on consistent defect logging, stable rating assumptions in FMEA, and sustained instructor/equipment control to avoid underestimating risk.
